title: Can a style travel?
method: Nine prompt-only first passes with the built-in image_gen tool, without reference images or identity locking. Two later still-life edits use the earlier generated images. Digital interpretations, not physical prints. No separate paid API backend was used.
design: Three fixed style blocks crossed with the same three scene briefs. Composition can adapt to the medium; this is a limited exploratory comparison, not a controlled reproducibility benchmark.

styles.name: Carbon & citrus
styles.grammar: A sparse editorial drawing transferred through exhausted blue carbon paper onto clean bright white paper. Broken ultramarine-blue lines, pressure gaps, occasional faint double tracks and incomplete contours describe the scene. Large areas remain entirely untouched. Do not enclose every shape or shade skin, fabric or objects. Faces, if present, use a few unequal strokes without rendered eyes, eyelashes, cheeks or hair strands. Hands are readable through their meeting edges, not detailed fingers. Every mark is a line except ONE flat, opaque vermilion-orange accent on the object specified in the scene. That accent is the only solid colour. No blue filled silhouettes, gray shadows, wash, pencil shading, cartoon prettiness, picturesque setting, paper stains or all-over texture. The incomplete drawing and solid accent are the grammar; no orange fruit is required.

styles.name: Stencil + red pencil
styles.grammar: An original hybrid editorial illustration on clean bright white. Broad flat dark petrol-green shapes are cut with reusable industrial stencils. Preserve clean narrow white support bridges that interrupt enclosed stencil forms. Use these rigid masses for clothing, major objects or supporting structures. A thin fragile dry RED COLOUR PENCIL line supplies small specific observations: profiles, the meeting of hands, a bent leaf or an object's rim. Red line has its own job; it does not trace every green silhouette. Keep faces unmodelled and hair a simple stencil shape. The single designated scene accent is one opaque burnt-orange area. Clean white gaps and a strong asymmetrical composition do the rest. No gray modelling, realistic faces, soft gradients, red cheek hatching, all-over grain, spray paint, splashes, military lettering, decorative faux misregistration or nostalgia. The large green template and the small red observation must remain visibly different tools.

styles.name: White-line engraving
styles.grammar: A one-colour black relief impression interpreted as fine white-line engraving cut with a burin into end-grain boxwood. Build from solid BLACK; light is made by fine WHITE incisions. Vary spacing, direction and the length of cuts according to the form. Short wedge cuts and uncut dark areas must alternate with restrained groups of curving fine furrows. Keep broad dark masses and decisive uncut silences; do not coat every surface in perfectly uniform contour bands. Faces and hands are observed but not glamorous. A mundane action can have the gravity of an emblem. Edges and form come from white cuts, not black pencil contours over white. The designated coloured accent in the subject must translate into a particularly clear white shape, because this entire image is MONOCHROME. No orange ink, grey wash, photographic grayscale, fine-line filter pasted over a photo, visible woodgrain across the artwork, antique-paper stains, sepia, ornamental borders or nostalgic costume.

scenes.name: Three neighbours
scenes.accent: the folded bag on the lowest step
scenes.brief: Three adult neighbours having an ordinary conversation on a broad front step. An older woman sits on the upper step at left, a heavy-set middle-aged man leans against a plain doorframe at right, and a young adult with a shaved head sits sideways one step lower. One speaks with a small open-hand gesture, the other two listen. They wear ordinary contemporary clothes. A small folded shopping bag rests on the lowest step. No tea cups, flowers, street scenery or symbolic decorations. Keep all three people recognisable as separate bodies and make the gestures quiet, not a posed group portrait. The designated accent is the folded bag.

scenes.name: A bicycle, together
scenes.brief: Two adults working together on an ordinary commuter bicycle in a plain small yard. One adult crouches at the rear wheel with a small orange-handled wrench; the other stands and steadies the saddle. Both are absorbed in the task, not smiling toward the viewer. The bicycle has two visibly distinct wheels, a plausible connected frame, one saddle and handlebars. Let the relationship between working hands and rear axle read clearly, without trying to turn this into a technical instruction diagram. No extra tools, helmet, plants, workbench or yard scenery. The designated accent is the small wrench handle.

scenes.name: Kettle, cloth, pear
scenes.accent: one broad folded edge of the dishcloth
scenes.brief: An object-only still life on a bare tabletop: a dented enamel kettle with its handle and short spout, a folded striped dishcloth, and one lopsided pear with a short bent stem. No people, hands, faces, windows or additional objects. Arrange the three objects so their unequal gaps matter. The kettle is the largest form; the pear is slightly apart from it. Avoid a tasteful staged kitchen or decorative background. The designated accent is one broad folded edge of the dishcloth, NOT the pear or kettle. The cloth needs only a suggestion of two stripes, not a decorative pattern.

revisions.prompt: Edit the supplied stencil + red-pencil still life. Preserve the square crop, kettle at left, pear at right, folded striped cloth below, petrol-green / red-pencil / burnt-orange / clean-white palette, and every object's position and scale. Remove the cosmetic wear from the image. Eliminate the scattered white chips, scraped patches, jagged flaked edges and random scratches from the kettle body, handle and pear. Make the large petrol-green areas smooth and opaque. Keep the kettle's one broad dent in its overall contour; do not add surface marks to explain it. Express the reusable stencil construction using a few clean straight white support bridges in the handle ring and where a closed interior needs support. These bridges are deliberate unpainted cuts, not chipped enamel. Keep the red pencil only at the kettle rim, spout lip and pear stem; remove incidental red tracing around most of the pear's perimeter. Keep the two green cloth stripes and its one solid orange folded edge, with plain white fabric between. No new objects, shadows, lettering or decorative texture. The intent is a crisp reusable shape grammar with small specific red observations, without a distressed-print costume. The supplied image is the edit target.
revisions.purpose: Remove cosmetic wear. Result also smoothed the edge character.

revisions.prompt: Image 1 is the edit target: the clean green stencil still life. Image 2 is a material-edge reference only: the first, rougher version of the same still life. Keep Image 1's exact objects, placement, large clear green shapes, white support bridges and orange cloth fold. Restore the distinction between an imperfect physical tool and an ideal vector path, WITHOUT restoring the chips or scattered wear from Image 2. Change only the edges and red pencil marks. Green edges should show the small, occasional blunt compression of a hand-cut card stencil: a short straight segment that meets a curve at an unequal angle, a tiny pigment bleed on one edge, a slight variation at the spout lip. The interiors remain opaque unshaded green and the entire paper remains clean white. Do not distress them. Use an actual-looking thin red coloured-pencil line whose pressure fades, breaks over the paper tooth, and briefly doubles back at the kettle rim, spout lip and pear stem. These few lines are fragile, partial observations and must not become a continuous red vector outline. Remove most of the red lower lid ring; leave only two short unequal red observations there. The contrast is a blunt reusable stencil and a searching pencil. Keep the cloth orange and the two cloth stripes intact, with an occasional direct uneven cut at the folded edge. No additional objects, drop shadows, surface modelling, speckles, fake aging or new colors. Maintain the overall simplicity.
revisions.purpose: Restore blunt edge changes and partial red observations without restoring surface wear. Red pencil remains more uniform than requested.

delivered.format: JPEG copies; originals retained in generation output
